title: revert(cli): stage os skills writes and swap them in by rename, recording last (#35495)
body:
Fixes #35588

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 用户能看到什么变化:用命令行安装或更新技能包的开发者,回到上一个发布版的写入方式:更新中途失败(磁盘满、权限不足)时,技能目录可能新旧混杂,要再强制更新一次才能恢复。
- 为什么做:为主干每四小时一次的全量检查解决变红,它被技能写入新加的暂存目录卡住;按席位指令先撤回那次改动,让主干恢复全绿。
- 出错会怎样:本次只删不增,和原改动逐字节相反,影响只在技能安装与更新两条命令;万一有问题,可以直接撤回本次撤回。
- 要你做什么:无

## This is a revert

This PR reverts #35495 (578d3b1d66) and nothing else. The diff is byte-identical to the inverse of that commit (`cmp` of the two patches, exit 0).

**Why.** #35495 added a staging directory, `mkdtempSync(join(dir, SKILLS_STAGING_PREFIX))` in `applySkillsWrite`. Its base `dir` is the caller's skills directory, which is cwd-relative (`resolveSkillsDir(args.dir, cwd)`). The dispatch-gates scratch-dir scan reads one file at a time and treats a cwd-relative base as unreadable on purpose, so the self-test case "no mkdtempSync site in this tree takes a base the scan cannot read" fails on that line. That one case of 2564 is what keeps main's scheduled full Lint & Type Check run red (#35588). No honest spelling inside the CLI file lets the scan read that base. Every spelling that turns the case green does so by a lie (a `tmpdir()` marker, a fabricated binding) or an evasion (`mkdirSync`, an aliased import), and the gate is not narrowed. The measurements are on #35588 (comment 7016701837). The seat ordered this revert as the named fallback.

**What returns.** The defect #35079 addressed comes back: an `os skills install` or `os skills update` that fails partway (disk full, permission, a locked file) can again leave the skill directories gone or half-written under the old record, and the next plain `update` refuses them as changed locally until `--force`. #35079 reopens.

**Re-landing.** The staged swap re-lands only after a gate-side ruling on how the scan judges a directory-creating call whose base is a caller's argument. Even a cross-file hop ends at `process.cwd()`, and a killed run at this repo's root would leave `.claude/skills/.objectstack-skills-staging-*`, which no tracked ignore rule covers. So the rule needs a policy, not a reading. That decision is outside this PR, and `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` is untouched.

## DELIBERATE CORRECTION

This PR deletes one pending release note it did not add: `.changeset/35079-skills-write-staged-swap.md`. It was never released. The behaviour it describes is the code this PR reverts, so the note would now be false. Its headline sentence, quoted as it stood on the merge base: "`os skills install` and `os skills update` stage the new catalog and swap it in by rename, so a write that fails partway leaves the previous skills and their record as they were". Corrected to: no note. With the note gone, the published `@objectstack/cli` never carried the staged swap, so this PR releases nothing and adds no changeset of its own. `skip-changeset` is not applied (ruling D on #18375). `Check Changeset` stays red by design (route 0 of its refusal text), and the dispatching seat confirms this correction by its own record.

## What changes

- `packages/cli/src/utils/skills-install-state.ts`: `applySkillsWrite` goes back to the pre-#35495 write (remove the dropped and replaced skill directories, write the new ones, write the record last). `SKILLS_STAGING_PREFIX`, the staging directory, the rename swap and its undo are removed.
- `packages/cli/test/skills-commands.test.ts`: the `an interrupted write leaves the installed catalog usable` block and the `node:fs` fault injection that served it are removed with the code they pinned.
- `.changeset/35079-skills-write-staged-swap.md`: deleted (see above).

## Read first

1. `packages/cli/src/utils/skills-install-state.ts`, the `applySkillsWrite` hunk: the riskiest change, the non-atomic write coming back.
2. `packages/cli/test/skills-commands.test.ts`: the deleted interrupted-write block. Every remaining test passes unchanged.
3. `.changeset/35079-skills-write-staged-swap.md`: the deletion the correction above declares.

## Two-minute verification

From the repo root on this branch:

```sh
node --input-type=module -e "const m = await import('./scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs'); const u = m.exposedScratchDirs({}).unresolved.filter(function (s) { return s.call === 'mkdtempSync'; }); console.log(u.length); process.exit(u.length ? 1 : 0);"
```

Expect `0` and exit 0. On `main` the same command prints `1` and exits 1.

## Tests

All readings below are on head `dc83a28e`. Exit codes were captured before any pipe.

<details>
<summary>The red case, before and after</summary>

- Before, at `e35cf035`, where `packages/cli/src/utils/skills-install-state.ts` is byte-identical to the merge base `f981dce3` (`git diff --quiet` exit 0). `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --self-test` (both tiers) printed `✗ no mkdtempSync site in this tree takes a base the scan cannot read — UNRESOLVED: packages/cli/src/utils/skills-install-state.ts:246 (dir is not bound in this file)` and `✗ dispatch-gates self-test: 1 of 2564 case(s) failed.`, exit 1.
- After: the one-case replay through the module's own `exposedScratchDirs` on this tree read sites=3127, inTree=93, exposed=0, unresolved(mkdtempSync)=0, exit 0. The classifier on the file alone gives 1 unresolved `mkdtempSync` site at base `f981dce3` (`:246 dir is not bound in this file`) and 0 at `dc83a28e`.
- The full self-test on `dc83a28e` was still running when this PR opened. Its verdict follows in the os-dev-report on #35588.

</details>

<details>
<summary>cli tests and typecheck</summary>

- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 test/skills-commands.test.ts`: `Test Files 1 passed (1)`, `Tests 30 passed (30)`, lock VERDICT command-exit 0.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli exec vitest run --project unit --maxWorkers=2`: `Test Files 431 passed (431)`, `Tests 6158 passed (6158)`, lock VERDICT command-exit 0. The integration layer is left to CI: the diff touches no integration file and no spawn entry.
- `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit && check:test-typecheck`): lock VERDICT command-exit 0, `check:test-typecheck: OK`.
- Dependency closure first: `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@objectstack/cli^...' build`, VERDICT command-exit 0, then `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli build`, VERDICT command-exit 0.

</details>

## Acceptance notes

- The case runs in the slow tier, so a pull request's own `Lint & Repo Gates` run (fast tier) does not execute it. The local full self-test under Tests is the evidence, and the next scheduled full run refreshes #35588.
- Observation, not filed: the scan holds the completeness rule to the spelling `mkdtempSync` only. Async `mkdtemp(join(PKG, 'tmp', ...))` builds in-tree fixture roots it does not see (`packages/cli/src/utils/graft-runtime-hooks.test.ts:236`, `packages/cli/test/next-steps.test.ts:83`). Both are covered by `.gitignore` `tmp/`, so nothing is exposed.

## Verification

The PR opened while the local gate runs were still finishing, so the local readings follow in the os-dev-report on #35588. CI on this PR is the gate.

- Derived set: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` gives 64 commands for this change set (3 paths vs merge base `f981dce3`). They run locally, byte for byte, and are reconciled with `--ran`.
- Expected red, by design: `node scripts/check-empty-changeset.mjs --base origin/main` exits 1 on the deleted foreign changeset (the DELIBERATE CORRECTION class above), and so does `Check Changeset` on this PR.
- `check:pm-dispatch-gates` on a pull request runs its fast tier only, so the red case is not in this PR's check-runs. The full self-test above is the reading for it.
